posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
I'm going to put this out there briefly and then try to get the thread relatively back on topic, as this is a board about superhero card games, not LGBT representation.  There are plenty of LGBT people in the world; I am proud to be one.  There are plenty of black, Hispanic, Asian, what-have-you people as well.  The comic book industry (and the archetypes that they ape) often strays way too far towards catering to the tastes of straight, white, middle-class men.  Any inclusion of characters that are not straight, white men is all right by me, because it's a step towards realism.  It's not pandering to have strong empowered heroes.  It's not pandering to include developed, nuanced characters who deal with their ethnicity or their sexuality in a mature manner.   And, above all else, >G have done a pretty solid job in diversifying a notoriously non-diverse segment of entertainment.

 

Now, back to real discussion!

I said:

  • Some type of Hawkeye/Green Arrow archer character.

Well, Parse definitely fits that mold.  I like the idea of a data analyst/hacker opposing the "bureaucratic" villain of Miss Information, but the Archery theme seems a little light on her.   Obviously I haven't seen the cards--I'm not a playtester--but when I picture Green Arrow or Hawkeye, I picture lots of gimmick arrows:  line arrows, explosive-tipped arrows, sonic stunner arrows, etc.  I'm kind of ambivalent about Parse's costume, though I do like the archery gauntlets, which look like she stole them from Hawkeye, as drawn by David Aja.

I said:

  • Some type of shapeshifty Beast Boy-type character.

Hit the nail on the head with this one!  The Naturalist certainly fits this mold perfectly.  I'm not sure what to think of his links to Akash'Bhuta and Argent Adept, but it feels like his background apes that of Black Panther or Moon Knight, which I like.  I'm interested to see what each of his forms will bring.  I'd assume that Rhinoceros and Crocodile are both forms, as they're mentioned directly in the text, though I'd like to see what else is in that deck.  Perhaps a constrictor-snake form to immobilize a villain target and keep them from dealing damage?  A bird-type card could scout the Environment or Villain decks, perhaps?  Lots of options here.

I said: 

  • "Twitchy", with some kind of probability control (he'll have the dice icon as his)

Got this one, too!  While I didn't bank on Setback having so many links to Baron Blade (apparently trying to create his own Legacy-type character), a bad-luck controlling character seems pretty awesome.  My wife once played an ICONS game as a bad-luck controller named Murphy...it was a blast!

  • A size-changing female Thorathian, a la Giganta.

Wow, was I ever off.  I didn't see this one coming at all, though having an actual FILTER agent (even a former one) as a hero makes sense.  KNYFE feels a lot like a mash-up of Black Widow and Psylocke to me, both of which are characters that don't get their due in the comics world.  Plus, I love the idea of a female character being a strong, melee bruiser:  it's just not something that you see often enough.  I wonder if the >G gang has been reading Deconnick's run on Captain Marvel, mayhaps?

I said:

Ooh, I forgot about biker guy!

I'm betting he'll be Mainstay--the enigmatic 5th from my list above.  I'd put money on him being a Lobo/Ghost Rider type dude--lots of chains, hooks, and knives, with some type of motorcycle or other vehicle, which could be represented like Turret Mode or Pushing the Limits.  I'd also bank on him having a lot of one-shots, instead of ongoings.  

So, I sort of got this one.  Mainstay sure is one of The Sentinels, but I expected him to be a bigger loner, much less a part of a whole team.  It's a neat twist, to me, to include him as a big, friendly sort of guy.  I'm not sure how the 4-in-1 deck is going to pan out, especially as compared to Baron Blade's Vengeance Party Smackdown.  I did have to laugh to see Dr. Medico make an appearance, and I see some neat synergy between Mainstay, Medico, and The Idealist (tank, healer, blaster).  My question is:  where does Writhe fit in?  Maybe he offers more of a control element?  I'm not sure how you'd implement intangibility into game play.

 

So, tally me up for 3.5 out of 5?  I only have a handful of ideas on the Villain/Environment decks, so here goes those:

  • We'll finally see the Evil Chinese Mystic-guy who Mister Fixer fights on some of his cards.  He'll be a Mandarin homage, I think, perhaps with a bunch of ninjas.  (Oooh, ninjas!  We haven't fought ninjas yet!  Gotta fight some ninjas!)
  • I see Baron Blade's Vengeance Party Bus playing much like The Ennead--5 character cards in play simultaneously, all of whom get to do wicked things on the Villain turn.  I don't see them being separable.
  • We haven't seen a cyborg-type character yet, aside from Golem Unity.  Some kind of cybernetic person, maybe?
  • I think we might actually get to fight in Baron Blade's Vengeance Party Garage, a la the Legion of Doom's big skull-head fortress.
  • A temple or the like might be cool to fight Evil Chinese Mystic-guy in...or maybe a pagoda!
  • How about on a ship or an aircraft carrier?  Or, perhaps, an homage to the Shield Helicarrier?

Rabit:

Not really. It can be a symptom, but many people manifest differently. My nephew has full-on autism, and most autistics do not like contact with people - they just can't stand it. My nephew is completely the opposite: he loves hugs, holding hands, jumping on his uncle's stomach (ugh - he's a heavy kid, takes after his dad). These diseases don't manifest in a "standard" way (unfortunately ).

Hm. Actually, I think it is a diagnostic marker, rather than just a symptom. That is, it is so prevalent among those with Asperger that it is a diagnostic criteria rather than an incidental finding, so if Parse doesn't exhibit it, it may be a case of misdiagnosis. Of course, by prevalent I mean about 80-90%, so it IS still possible. In this case, there is a common/'standard' neural pathway that is hit in the syndrome, making their proprioception, er, skewey. More likely, Parse has some degree of severity of autism, rather than out-and-out Asperger.

Err, normally, I would just leave things like this be (I mean, can you say off topic?), but I really don't like it when people take a disease entity and lump them all together as the same thing (i.e. Asperger is just fancy autism.) Of course, I fully expect that this was not intended, but still. No harm in correcting? D:

 

I agree with the rest of your points, btw :))

 

Edit: I would like to point out this study Journal of Developmental & Behavioral Pediatrics Specifically: "It has been estimated that 80% of subjects with AS display "motor dyspraxia," or clumsiness"

 

Edit2: TheJayMann, Thank you for sharing! I…am now thoroughly confused. Oh well. Must study harder!

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Okay, so I'm pretty excited by the new heroes. I like the look/sound of every single one of them from what we've seen so far.

KNYFE: Yay! Our first British hero! The energy blades look cool and as others have said it's nice to have a (presumably) hitting-things-hard female character. And it's interesting that she's involved in all that timey-wimey stuff too. I'm already practicing my Scottish accent.

Sentinels: I do wish they'd been given a different name, due to the game name, but I like the way the group fits together and the idea of a team is great. I'm amused that the Medico joke is now a thing and Mainstay seems fun. The Idealist - superhero kid, interesting! And Writhe, again I'd have preferred a different name since it's so close to Wraith, but I'm looking forward to seeing how his shadowiness will work.

Naturalist: Possibly my favourite concept so far. I think (and I may be wrong) that he's the first African hero. The whole shape-shifting thing is a great idea and the tension between him and AA make me wonder if that'll be reflected in the gameplay somehow. I can't see them playing well together.

Setback: I'm not normally keen on extra luck in games, but if there's an element of luck to the way he plays then I'm definitely looking forward to seeing how he works. I think he has the clearest "voice" so far and I love that his bio gives us so much information on what his personality's like.

Parse: Yay, archery is awesome! Also black, Australian, female, with a condition that is generally considered a disability. I totally approve of the inclusion of groups that are traditionally under-represented in the genre. It'd be easy for Kim to be another white American, and we have a lot of those already. Interestingly enough, if she's represented as an Australian Aborigine (even better) then that's another little link to her powers - Australian Aborigines have significantly better spacial memory compared with their white cohorts (probably due to aspects of upbringing, since it's an important skill for a group that traditionally had to be skilled at wayfaring in a hostile, somewhat barren desert environment). And I like the Omnitron connection too.

In general, I like how so many things are starting to get tied into other things, like Setback and Blade, Naturalist and Akash and Argent, KNYFE and FILTER, Parse and Cosmitron. We have some answers, and a lot more questions, and I'm even more excited for what's coming next! Thanks >G, you guys rule! :)

Ronway:

Well, Parse may be a bit clusmy, possibly not even the best with a bow. Silverleaf pointed out that she is wearing an archery glove (forgot the name of it), which is worm be folks to protect their arm from the bow string hitting it. Or it could be that she just wants to wear it, who really knows?

Trust me, it hurts after you've done that 10 times or so. Last time I shot (a while ago) I developed a large bruise the whole way down the inside of my forearm, and I don't bruise easily, and that was just with a relatively puny 35lb shortbow.

As for manual dexterity, it comes in lots of different forms and skills can obviously be trained. I'd guess Parse is good at archery more because of her ability to calculate the trajectory, distance, angles, draw distance on the arrow, speed or target, etc., than her natural physical ability. She only has to be competant in the physical sighting, drawing and releasing which just really requires conditioning and practice.

posts.cooked:
Ronway:

Well, Parse may be a bit clusmy, possibly not even the best with a bow. Silverleaf pointed out that she is wearing an archery glove (forgot the name of it), which is worm be folks to protect their arm from the bow string hitting it. Or it could be that she just wants to wear it, who really knows?

 

I've been shooting arrows at targets for about 10 years now, and the glove/wrist guard are essential.  even with calusses to protect your fingers, its really nice to have something between them and a bowstring.  Especially with heavier short/recurve bows (which is what Parse is using, rather than a composite).  the wrist guard is more useful when you are learning (I used to have bruises and welts from the string hitting my arm, even with the guard), but it also serves the prosaic function of keeping your sleeves/coat/etc out of the way.  Also it looks cool.

Or hey, maybe she has an touchscreen computer on the outside!
